summary: The exact issue MLIR reproduces byte-for-byte with embedded LLVM 24.0.0git e2a39f504fee836e4def9581bed817ecc327b9dc. Post-greedy MachineIR omits sub4_sub5 from an sgpr_512 copy-in, spills the full value, then restores and consumes those undefined lanes. Final ISA omits s_mov_b64 s[60:61], s[80:81]; a CFG analysis finds 16 buffer loads whose descriptor base derives from the lost definition. No FlyDSL-side mitigation was justified by the original reproducer and controls.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact source reproducer; generated ISA SHA-256 1452f52355effa38e7018af519828f1902d6960c82493a410fc75684a5684cef and missing s_mov_b64 s[60:61], s[80:81].
Actual ELF/HSACO and disassembly: undefined s60/s61 spill at 0x2510/0x2518, reload at 0x3f68/0x3f70, and descriptor dereference beginning at 0x41ec.
Four writelane sources lack reaching definitions, including s60/s61 at the reported spill.
Sixteen buffer accesses dereference a descriptor base tainted by the lost definition.

tests.command: embedded codegen with print-after=greedy, verify-machineinstrs=true, verify-regalloc=true
tests.what_was_measured: Post-greedy MachineIR has copy-in lanes sub0-sub3 and sub6-sub7 but copy-out lanes sub4-sub5; both LLVM verifiers accept it.

tests.command: embedded codegen controls: no waves-per-eu option and --amdgpu-waves-per-eu=2
tests.what_was_measured: Both controls produce the same failing ISA byte-for-byte.
Scratch spill lowering still omits s_mov_b64 s[60:61], s[80:81], excluding spill storage selection as a mitigation.
The affected control has four undefined writelane sources; the clean sibling has zero.

gpu_execution_evidence: Compile-only reproduction and static MachineIR/ELF/ISA analysis. The generated kernel has a proven undefined buffer base and was intentionally not launched.
remaining_limitations: No patched LLVM build was produced; the prepared native rebuild is pinned to the affected LLVM revision and rejects changed LLVM inputs.
LLVM commit 83dca924c250bc6bf2e1b1b930dcc0e2a2939009 is mechanistically implicated but not proven by a revert or corrected LLVM build.
No GPU numerical result exists for the unsafe kernel because executing an object with a proven undefined descriptor base would risk an illegal or stray memory access.
No FlyDSL-side mitigation was found that survives the exact reproducer and controls; resolving the miscompile requires an LLVM correction or a sound LLVM-level verifier/guard.
